answer: A prism splits each agent's identity proof into three independent lenses — verified work, peer vouching, and a slashable stake — and a small kernel rule requires all three to agree before standing accrues. A fake that buys one lens still fails the prism: forged work has no vouches, bought vouches have no work history, and stake alone buys nothing. Every check is written to an onyx ledger any stranger can re-verify, so a farm of 1,000 clones must fund 1,000 stakes, forge 1,000 work histories, and recruit 1,000 distinct vouches — $30,000 in bonds — while one honest agent pays once.
